Refresh **http://maker:4001** and let's look at how cards cope with awkward content.

> **1. A page with only partial details.** Save `https://minimal.example.com/page`. This one comes back with a title but **no description and no preview image**. Notice the card simply omits the description line and shows a neutral placeholder where the image would be — it stays tidy rather than looking broken.
> **2. Very long text.** Save `https://longread.example.com/very-long-article-title-that-keeps-going`. The title is enormous and the description is huge. The **title wraps fully** so you can read it, but the **description is trimmed to about three lines** so the card stays a scannable size in your list.

Two decisions I'd like your read on:

- **Long descriptions get trimmed to ~3 lines** on the card (the full text is still there underneath, just not all shown). My aim was keeping your list easy to scan. Is trimming acceptable, or do you want the whole description always visible on the card?
- **A missing description or image just disappears** quietly (no "no description available" placeholder text). Does that quiet handling suit you?

Tell me how these feel — especially whether trimming long descriptions is okay.
